methods.name: YOLO
methods.description_short: A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation.

evidence.quote: We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to per-form detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a re-gression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network pre-dicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation.

methods.name: Fast YOLO
methods.description_short: A smaller version of the YOLO network that processes images at 155 frames per second.

evidence.quote: A smaller version of the network, Fast YOLO, processes an astounding 155 frames per second while still achieving double the mAP of other real-time detec-tors.

methods.name: YOLO Detection System
methods.description_short: Processing images with YOLO is simple and straightforward.

evidence.quote: Processing images with YOLO is simple and straightforward. Our system (1) resizes the input image to 448 × 448, (2) runs a single convolutional net-work on the image, and (3) thresholds the resulting detections by the model’s confidence.

methods.name: YOLO Model
methods.description_short: A single convolutional network simultaneously predicts multiple bounding boxes and class probabilities for those boxes.

evidence.quote: YOLO is refreshingly simple: see Figure 1. A sin- gle convolutional network simultaneously predicts multi- ple bounding boxes and class probabilities for those boxes.
For evaluating YOLO on PASCAL VOC, we useS = 7, B = 2. PASCAL VOC has 20 labelled classes so C = 20.
We pretrain our convolutional layers on the ImageNet 1000-class competition dataset [30].
